sourceInformation.perspective: Side-on, whole-room 2D camera with native projected 3D characters
sourceInformation.tech: my-3d2dge 0.89.1; AI Hub Session Protocol 1 / client 1.4.0; JavaScript, Canvas 2D and Web Audio; Node 24.21.0 build; Playwright 1.63.0 tests
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original procedural pixel mine; timber, work lamps, mineral seams, three ore silhouettes, custom doors and miner equipment using native shapes and materials
sourceInformation.animation: Native Humanoid rigs, Platformer traversal, Attack phases, custom hat/weapon hooks and 11 original held poses
sourceInformation.audio: Original coded chip music, procedural mining effects and formant gibberish; separate music/SFX/voice buses; music defaults to 10%; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: One or two players in AI Hub shared-world co-op, including nonplayer authority; solo and simultaneous two-player local co-op standalone
sourceInformation.testing: Unrestricted native headless and scripted browser tests; emulated standard controllers and touch; offline Web Audio measurements; no physical controller, real iOS device, TV or listening panel
sourceInformation.research: Original US manual and archived mine/doorway screenshots confirmed; supplied 1982 review URL returned 404; precise original audio unknown. Sources and adaptations documented in docs/research.md
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux / Ubuntu on WSL2

testingFeedback: 23 unique issues caught by automated checks, visual checks and integration review; all fixed. The ledger separates review findings from reproduced test failures.
9 critical issues affected launch, required controls, progression or simultaneous local co-op; all fixed.
Long hidden-authority shared-world playthroughs exposed delayed feedback and lost press direction that short protocol checks missed.
Syntax-only checks were least helpful for gameplay: they cannot establish traversal, recovery, co-op ownership or completion.
engineFeedback: Native platformer physics, posed humanoids and the shape/material registry made a cohesive game possible without image assets.
Native crouch consumed down before ladder descent. A contextual adapter reserves down at a ladder top; exact APIs were checked in the handoff.
The deterministic rock/supply director and authenticated shared-world replication were the largest game-specific systems.
Keeping native traversal, temporary topology, action timing and visual contact points consistent across headless and rendered copies.
None. The vendored engine and released Hub client are unmodified; game-specific extensions use native hooks.
Expose a compact serializable Platformer traversal state with a tested prediction/reconciliation example.
promptFeedback: The director plan gives concrete mechanics, recovery rules and acceptance evidence while leaving room for original art and branding.
Standalone online could imply matchmaking; the plan resolves this as local co-op standalone and online shared-world co-op through Hub.
Integrating the whole expedition, resource fairness, controller/touch UX and hidden Hub authority into one portable HTML.
Separate required release gates from aspirational first-run pacing, and include a small official shared-world serialization example.

aiHub.name: Pick Axe Deplete
aiHub.description: Turn an unruly mine into one last spectacular payday. Chop ore, engineer ricochets, chase falling picks and rising keys, and prime three extraction machines alone or with a partner.
aiHub.controls: A/D or arrows move; W/S climb or duck; Space jump; J/click chop; Q/right-click redirect; E door/rescue; Escape pause. Standard gamepad and assisted multitouch supported.
